results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 51 outline summaries match the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph, in spec order; the three opening callouts match no paragraph.

results.draft_locus: Adyen's Route: One Banking License, Extended by Branches ¶3
results.quote: What it does publish runs the other way
results.finding: The unit holds two ideas: where Adyen's route stops (84% full-stack, partner banks where it has no license) and what Adyen does and does not publish about acquiring entities and network memberships per country. The spec's controlling idea for p30 joins the same two with 'and', and both flow readers lost the paragraph's main point at the pivot.
Every unit ties to a supporting claim S1 to S6 or is declared context or transition (p04, p05, p51).

results.draft_locus: Adyen's Route: One Banking License, Extended by Branches ¶3
results.quote: Its documentation says that "Pass-through payout is the only available payout model in Africa, Brazil, and India" (n.d., accessed November 2026).
results.finding: The fact is followed by 'And it publishes no list...'; no sentence says what it shows (the spec's 'shows': settlement works differently in markets outside the core licenses). Both flow readers noted the sentence does not say what it shows about the acquirer. All other evidence items, tables and figures are explained by an adjacent sentence or caption.

results.draft_locus: What the Acquirer of Record Changes: Domestic Payments and an Unmeasured Uplift ¶1
results.quote: Start with what "domestic" means to a network.
results.finding: The declared cause_effect transition should pick up the acquirer of record as a legal fact separate from the connection and introduce what that fact changes. The opening changes subject to 'domestic' without picking up the acquirer, which returns only a paragraph later ('The acquirer enters through a second rule'); only the heading states the link. All other declared transitions are expressed at their boundaries.

results.draft_locus: Adyen's Route: One Banking License, Extended by Branches ¶1
results.quote: Adyen is the documented case of the third route.
results.finding: Both flow readers describe the organising principle as general-to-particular in prerequisite order, which agrees with the declared pattern, but both mark the position of the Adyen section as unclear: the routes are taught sponsor bank, narrow license, bank license, and the cases then start with the third. The spec's flow rationale gives no reason for Adyen before Stripe that the prose could state.
results.corroborated_by: second flow reader, part 2 item 6 (and reordering item 1); reported by first flow reader, part 2 item 7

results.draft_locus: Two Permissions: A Network Membership and a License ¶1

results.finding: The scene heading promises 'Two Words' that the scene never names ("local acquiring"), and one section later a different pair ("Member", "Indirectly") is said to carry the chapter; both readers went back to check whether they were the same words.
results.corroborated_by: second flow reader, item 5 (first flow reader, item 3)

The introduction opens on a dated puzzle of two true statements, states stakes and thesis, and gives a roadmap; none of the weak patterns applies.

The conclusion sorts its points by how settled they are, labels the author's position, and adds no new subtopic or body evidence; it does not open with 'in conclusion' or end on a rephrased thesis alone.

The author's synthesis states what no single section states ('which provider' is a commercial question, 'which acquirer in this country' the operative one, because membership, liability, first receipt of the money and domestic status attach to the acquirer) and the questions turn it into what a team does. The second half of the declared synthesis, that public claims attach to the provider, is implied and not stated.

results.draft_locus: Questions to Ask ¶1
results.quote: When the provider says "direct connection", does it mean it exchanges messages with the network, or that it is the member?
results.finding: The conclusion does not return to the introduction's two Stripe statements (direct integrations in 2020, bank acquirers in 2026). The explicit return is in the Stripe section ('Now the two statements from the introduction fit together'); in the conclusion only question 4 echoes the distinction, generically and without the opening pair.

From the introduction alone the reader predicted every section in the roadmap's order, the kinds of evidence (dated provider quotations, license facts, vendor figures read sceptically, the Larkfield case, a comparison) and the tone. Not predictable: which two words, the third route and the names of the two permissions.

The cold reader names the bank as acquirer of record (holds the membership, answers to the network, receives settlement first), reads 'direct integrations' as message exchange only that says nothing about who the member is, and adds what to ask next; nothing contradicts the expected answer.

The cold reader gives the figure no weight as a measure while accepting the direction: single customer, vendor-reported, several changes bundled, no baseline, no independent measurement of size, and lists what a sound measurement would hold constant.

results.draft_locus: Stripe and Adyen: Where They Differ ¶3
results.quote: Stripe's acquirer terms call its EEA entity and its US limited-purpose bank "a member of the Networks"
results.finding: The chapter does say in plain words where the public record stops, and nearly every company statement carries a year or access date inline. This statement about Stripe's EEA entity as a network member is new here and carries neither in the text; the access date of the STEL acquirer terms is given only in the source list.

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶4
results.quote: Studio Noord is on Adyen, so here it is Adyen N.V.; that is my reading of Adyen's license page
results.finding: A statement about Adyen's acquirer resting on its license page carries no year or access date; the page is first dated ('n.d., accessed November 2026') several sections later.
